summary: Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) worked in sinology and philosophy. Educated in Paris, he held posts at the National Museum of Vietnamese History, Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, École Pratique des Hautes Études, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and École Française d'Extrême-Orient.

Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Saigon and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and held a post at Vạn Hạnh University around 1974–1975.

M. A. Mehendale (1918–2020) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970 and 1983).
M. Athar Ali (1925–1998) was a historian who studied at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1948 to 1961 and served there as a historian from around 1953 to 1990.

M. D. Balasubrahmanyam specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing a dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University by 1969. He held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University, Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, and Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan.

M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner, he served as Professor of History, department head, and arts dean at Mysore.

M. M. McCabe (born 1948) is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She held positions at Murray Edwards College, King's College London as Professor, University College London, and Newnham College.

M. N. Srinivas (1916–1999) worked in sociology and Indology. Educated at Mysore, Mumbai under G. S. Ghurye, and Oxford, he held posts at Oxford, Baroda, Delhi University, and the Institute for Social and Economic Change.

M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he served as a professor at the University of Calicut.

M. S. A. Rao (1926–1985) studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held academic posts at the University of Delhi, Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, and as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.
M. Shinoda (born 1977) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami and completed education at Agoura High School and Art Center College of Design.

M. Yamunacharya (born 1898) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Bern under Edouard Müller-Hess and taught Pali at University College London and SOAS.

Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres and the University of Kerala under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri, and taught at École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Madhav Krishna Sharma was an Indologist who studied as a pupil under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1952, he served as an Inspector for the Department of Sanskrit Education, Rajasthan.

Madhav M. Deshpande (born 1946) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Michigan, with his tenure attested between 1976 and 2009.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. In 2012, she held posts attested at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky (1927–2016) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Fergusson College. He founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and held leadership roles at the American Institute of Indian Studies from 1966 to 2005.

Madhusudan Gupta (1800–1856) was an Indologist educated at Sanskrit College and University and Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata. He taught Ayurveda at Sanskrit College (~1830–1835) and held a post at Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata (~1835–1856).
